the red circle opens the EPA behind a margin or an Overs / Unders record; tap anywhere else on a game to open its page
ⓘ Legend
The dropdown: a red circle marks something that opens on a tap or click. On a game it shows the EPA comparison behind the model margin, the home-field step, the injuries that moved it and the adjusted margin. Tapping the game row anywhere else opens the game page: the projection, each offense against its defense, the starters, the injuries, the plan and the report. On an Overs or Unders record it lists the plan's calls on that side with the Normal / Edge / Edge+ rungs and, once played, what happened.
Line · O/U The closing spread from the favorite's side and the market total. Once played, the total shows the points and whether it went over or under. Shown for context: the engine prices player props, not sides.
Model The engine's own margin for the favorite, from its opponent-adjusted efficiency ratings entering the week. Green = the engine likes the favorite more than the line does; amber = it actually likes the dog.
Adj The model margin with the priced injury reports folded in. ↯ marks a game where the injuries flip the engine's side.
Proj · Score The projected score and the final, favorite first.
Overs · Unders The pre-game single-game parlay plan's player calls, split by side: hits–misses once the box score is in, call counts before. A void is a player who did not play.
Plan cushion Every call is read at three rungs of the player's Kalshi ladder. Normal is the line the plan called. Edge is the listed rung nearest halfway between that line and the ladder's last rung on the easy side. Edge+ is that last rung: the lowest N+ on an over, the highest <N on an under. The pills swap the Overs and Unders columns between them; the record beside each pill is the week's total at that cushion.
Report The post-game report's projection grade, shown once reports are written.
Sorting Click any column header to rank by it; click again to flip.

JAX@BAL⚠ QB BAL: Tyler Huntley Out TNF -8.5 40.5 43 over +0.4 +4.1 24–16 33–10
1–5
JAX @ BAL over calls · 6 · graded off the box score
Rashod Bateman BALover 14.5 rec ydsmiss · actual 6
His number is priced for the quarterback, not the role: he has been back to a full starter's snap share and led the team in air yards two weeks ago. Two catches clear it.
Normal15+ -107 ✗Edge10+ -161 ✗Edge+10+ -161 ✗
Brenton Strange JAXover 29.5 rec ydsmiss · actual 22
His line is set for a game where Jacksonville barely throws, but he is the first read in the short middle and the safety valve on third down. Four of his seven games have beaten this number.
Normal30+ -148 ✗Edge20+ -276 ✓Edge+10+ -788 ✓
Justice Hill BALover 2.5 receptionshit · actual 3
With a first-time starter under pressure and no run game to lean on, the back becomes the outlet. That is exactly what happened in his last two games, and this script is more extreme.
Normal3+ -142 ✓Edge2+ -322 ✓Edge+2+ -322 ✓
Trevor Lawrence JAXover 1.5 pass TDsmiss · actual 1
A finishing call, not a yardage one. Baltimore surrenders touchdowns on nearly two of three red-zone trips, and Jacksonville's scoring has come through the air even on tiny attempt counts.
Normal2+ -137 ✗Edge1+ -719 ✓Edge+1+ -719 ✓
Zay Flowers BALover 4.5 receptionsmiss · actual 3
He is the only route-winner on a team that will be throwing short and often from behind. Catch volume, not yardage, is the stable part of his profile with a replacement quarterback.
Normal5+ -116 ✗Edge3+ -489 ✓Edge+2+ -1236 ✓
Chris Rodriguez Jr. JAXover 29.5 rush ydsmiss · actual 19
The lead back did not practice all week on an ankle, and this is the game plan that produces 28-30 carries. Rodriguez also owns short yardage into a defense that concedes touchdowns inside the 20.
Normal30+ -126 ✗Edge20+ -276 ✗Edge+10+ -788 ✓
3–3
JAX @ BAL under calls · 6 · graded off the box score
Parker Washington JAXunder 59.5 rec ydsmiss · actual 61
His big games require Jacksonville throwing 39-41 times while behind. In every game they have controlled he has seen two to five targets, and this is the biggest control script of their season.
Normal<60 +105 ✗Edge<110 -609 ✓Edge+<160 -3476 ✓
Derrick Henry BALunder 69.5 rush ydshit · actual 57
The worst run matchup in football meets a team that will be trailing. Baltimore's ground game has produced negative value in four of its last five weeks, and a deficit takes the fourth-quarter carries away.
Normal<70 -107 ✓Edge<120 -788 ✓Edge+<160 -3476 ✓
Bhayshul Tuten JAXunder 89.5 rush+rec ydshit · actual 29
An ankle that kept him out of practice all week in a backfield that already splits work, against a front that holds backs under four yards a carry. The role is likely managed even if he plays.
Normal<90 ✓Edge<90 ✓Edge+<90 ✓
Jakobi Meyers JAXunder 39.5 rec ydsmiss · actual 65
A hamstring that had him limited all week on a receiver whose snap share already slid, inside an offense that may throw twenty times. His one big game came against his former team.
Normal<40 -116 ✗Edge<80 -660 ✓Edge+<110 -3476 ✓
Trevor Lawrence JAXunder 224.5 pass ydsmiss · actual 242
His attempts are a pure script variable and this is the script that caps them: with a two-score lead this offense runs and shortens the game rather than throwing.
Normal<225 +109 ✗Edge<300 -525 ✓Edge+<350 -1684 ✓
